correctness.rationale: For squarefree degree-twelve f, the genus is five and the involution quotient has genus two. An independent polynomial expansion gives the exactly diagonal five-by-five matrix with coefficients 3a,3(a²+1),a(a²−1),3(a²+1),3a. In characteristic seven, semilinearity preserves its zero/nonzero diagonal pattern, so stable Frobenius rank equals Hasse rank. The quotient differential eigenspace comprises entries 2 and 4, and the complementary Prym threefold the other entries, since the degree-two isogeny is prime to seven. The four disjoint parameter cases give all p-ranks and a-numbers. The rank-three a-number at a=0 proves Prym superspeciality. The standalone checker independently constructs f³ over F7 and F49 and reproduces all matrices/ranks. The claim excludes a²=4 and does not infer an infinite theorem solely from finite enumeration.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural one-dimensional locus of genus-five Jacobians with a specified extra involution, rather than an arbitrary coefficient slice. Its four rank strata 2,3,4,5 are all attained and none of 0,1 occur, with nonreduced Hasse determinant multiplicities (3,2,1) on the nonordinary locus. The geometric contribution is complementary exceptional behavior: an ordinary genus-two quotient with superspecial threefold Prym at a=0, versus a superspecial genus-two quotient with ordinary Prym at a²=-1. These determine distinct group-scheme geometries of the Prym and Jacobian in a canonical dihedral family, useful for studying Prym arithmetic. This precise classification is not provided by the general normal form or rank-existence result.
